findings.title: isAccessTokenId() grant-shortcut check is inverted and reads the wrong characters
findings.body:
The new matcher is supposed to assert that the `jti` of an access token encodes the expected grant shortcut. Two defects make it a no-op:

1. The condition is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` fails the match when the shortcut *matches* instead of when it differs.
2. The offsets are wrong. The encoded prefix is `<sessionType:2><tokenType:2><grantType:2>`, so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)`. `substring(3,5)` returns the second char of the token type plus the first char of the grant type (e.g. for `onrtac` it returns `"ta"`).

Because of (2) the comparison can never be true for any currently defined shortcut, so with (1) the method always falls through to the UUID check and never verifies the grant type at all. Every call site (`expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`) therefore silently passes, leaving the main new behaviour of this PR untested. Fixing only the offsets without fixing the inversion would invert all those assertions and break the suite.

findings.title: Null check for rawTokenId actually re-checks grantType
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` validates `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId`. As a result a `null` rawTokenId is accepted, and the failure only surfaces later as a token id literally ending in `":null"` produced by `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` (string concatenation of null), i.e. a corrupt `jti`, instead of failing fast at construction time with a clear message.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes on a NullPointerException, not on the intended validation error
findings.body: The test sets up the factory by calling only `init(null)` and populating the maps directly; `postInit()` is never called, so `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.sessionFactory` stays `null`. Decoding `"ofrtac:5678"` misses the cache and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` dereferences `sessionFactory`, throwing a `NullPointerException`. Since the test catches the broad `RuntimeException`, it passes for the wrong reason and never exercises the intended `IllegalArgumentException("...Unknown value 'ac' for grant type")` path. Assert on the concrete exception type and make the factory usable (or inject a session factory) so the real validation path is covered.

findings.title: getShortcut() javadoc says 3 letters, but the decoder requires exactly 2
findings.body: The javadoc states the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants", while `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` encodes/decodes a fixed 6-character prefix (2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type) and rejects anything else with `IllegalArgumentException("...Expected length of 6")`. A custom grant factory that follows the javadoc and returns a 3-character shortcut will produce token ids that this very provider cannot decode (and a 1-character shortcut would silently shift the grant type characters). Fix the javadoc to require exactly 2 characters and validate the length (and the absence of the `:` delimiter) in `postInit()` so misbehaving providers fail at boot rather than producing undecodable token ids.

findings.title: New abstract SPI method breaks existing grant-type factories and can fail server startup
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as a non-default abstract method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` SPI interface. Existing third-party grant type factories no longer compile and, if deployed as an already-compiled jar, will fail with `AbstractMethodError` when `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` iterates all grant factories. Additionally, `postInit()` puts the returned shortcut into a `ConcurrentHashMap` without a null check, so a provider returning `null` makes `postInit()` throw a bare `NullPointerException` and the whole server fails to boot with no indication of which provider is at fault; the same code also blindly casts every `ProviderFactory<OAuth2GrantType>` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, which would throw `ClassCastException` for a factory implementing only `ProviderFactory`. Consider a `default` implementation and defensive handling/validation in `postInit()`.

findings.title: Lazy shortcut-map refresh bypasses duplicate-shortcut validation and can map a shortcut to the wrong grant
findings.body: `postInit()` validates that no two grants share a shortcut (by comparing map sizes), but `getShortcutByGrantType()` and `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` later mutate the same maps at runtime for "newly deployed" grant types without re-running that validation. `getGrantTypeByShortcut()` simply takes `findFirst()` of all factories whose shortcut matches, and `getShortcutByGrantType()` unconditionally overwrites the `grantsByShortcuts` entry for that shortcut. If a newly registered grant collides with an existing shortcut, decoding a token id will silently resolve to the wrong grant type (and the reverse mapping becomes inconsistent) instead of being rejected.

findings.title: Format change of the access token `jti` is not documented / no upgrade note
findings.body: Every access token's `id` (`jti` claim, and the `token_id` event detail) changes from a plain UUID to `<6-char-context>:<uuid>`. This is a client-visible contract change: integrations that store `jti` in a UUID column, parse it with `UUID.fromString()`, or assume a 36-char value will break after upgrade. The PR contains no documentation or upgrading/release-note entry describing the new format, its stability guarantees, or the fact that old (pre-upgrade) tokens still carry a bare UUID that decodes to `UNKNOWN`. Add the corresponding documentation/upgrade note before merging.
